shlokas.sanskrit: तच्छ्रुत्वा लक्ष्मणेनोक्तं वाक्यं वाक्यविशारदः । प्रत्युवाच महातेजाः प्रहसन्राघवो वचः ।। 7.87.1 ।।
shlokas.transliteration: tacchrutvā lakṣmaṇenoktaṃ vākyaṃ vākyaviśāradaḥ | pratyuvāca mahātejāḥ prahasanrāghavo vacaḥ || 7.87.1 ||
shlokas.wordByWord: Hearing that speech uttered by Lakshmana, Raghava of great splendor, skilled in discourse, smiling, replied with these words.

shlokas.sanskrit: एवमेव नरश्रेष्ठ यथा वदसि लक्ष्मण । वृत्रघातमशेषेण वाजिमेधफलं च यत् ।। 7.87.2 ।।
shlokas.transliteration: evameva naraśreṣṭha yathā vadasi lakṣmaṇa | vṛtraghātamaśeṣeṇa vājimedhaphalaṃ ca yat || 7.87.2 ||
shlokas.wordByWord: It is exactly so, O best of men, as you say, Lakshmana — both the slaying of Vritra in its entirety and the fruit that is gained from the horse-sacrifice.

shlokas.sanskrit: श्रूयते हि पुरा सौम्य कर्दमस्य प्रजापतेः । पुत्रो बाह्लीश्वरः श्रीमानिलो नाम महाशयाः ।। 7.87.3 ।।
shlokas.transliteration: śrūyate hi purā saumya kardamasya prajāpateḥ | putro bāhlīśvaraḥ śrīmānilo nāma mahāśayāḥ || 7.87.3 ||
shlokas.wordByWord: For it is heard, O gentle one, that in olden times there was a son of Kardama the Prajapati, a glorious and high-minded lord of Bahlika named Ila.

shlokas.sanskrit: स राजा पृथिवीं सर्वां वशे कृत्वा सुधार्मिकः । राज्यं चैव नरव्याघ्र पुत्रवत्पर्यपालयत् ।। 7.87.4 ।।
shlokas.transliteration: sa rājā pṛthivīṃ sarvāṃ vaśe kṛtvā sudhārmikaḥ | rājyaṃ caiva naravyāghra putravatparyapālayat || 7.87.4 ||
shlokas.wordByWord: That most righteous king, having brought the whole earth under his sway, ruled his kingdom too, O tiger among men, as though it were his own son.

shlokas.sanskrit: सुरैश्च परमोदारैर्दैतेयैश्च महाधनैः । नागराक्षसगन्धर्वैर्यक्षैश्च सुमहात्मभिः ।। 7.87.5 ।।
shlokas.transliteration: suraiśca paramodārairdaiteyaiśca mahādhanaiḥ | nāgarākṣasagandharvairyakṣaiśca sumahātmabhiḥ || 7.87.5 ||
shlokas.wordByWord: By the most magnanimous gods, by the wealthy Daityas, by the Nagas, Rakshasas, and Gandharvas, and by the exceedingly great-souled Yakshas —

shlokas.sanskrit: पूज्यते नित्यशः सौम्य भयार्तै रघुनन्दन । अबिभ्यंश्च त्रयो लोकाः सरोषस्य महात्मनः ।। 7.87.6 ।।
shlokas.transliteration: pūjyate nityaśaḥ saumya bhayārtai raghunandana | abibhyaṃśca trayo lokāḥ saroṣasya mahātmanaḥ || 7.87.6 ||
shlokas.wordByWord: He was worshipped continually, O gentle delight of the Raghus, by those afflicted with fear; and the three worlds were terrified of that great-souled one whenever he was wrathful.

shlokas.sanskrit: स राजा तादृशो ह्यासीद्धर्मे वीर्ये च निष्ठितः । बुद्ध्या च परमोदारो बाह्लीकेशो महायशाः ।। 7.87.7 ।।
shlokas.transliteration: sa rājā tādṛśo hyāsīddharme vīrye ca niṣṭhitaḥ | buddhyā ca paramodāro bāhlīkeśo mahāyaśāḥ || 7.87.7 ||
shlokas.wordByWord: Such indeed was that king, firmly established in righteousness and in valor, most magnanimous in understanding — the illustrious lord of Bahlika of great renown.

shlokas.sanskrit: स प्रचक्रे महाबाहुर्मृगयां रुचिरे वने । चैत्रे मनोरमे मासि सभृत्यबलवाहनः ।। 7.87.8 ।।
shlokas.transliteration: sa pracakre mahābāhurmṛgayāṃ rucire vane | caitre manorame māsi sabhṛtyabalavāhanaḥ || 7.87.8 ||
shlokas.wordByWord: That mighty-armed one undertook a hunt in a lovely forest, in the delightful month of Chaitra, together with his attendants, his army, and his mounts.

shlokas.sanskrit: प्रजघ्ने च नृपो ऽरण्ये मृगाञ्छतसहस्रशः । हत्वैव तृप्तिर्नाभूच्च राज्ञस्तस्य महात्मनः ।। 7.87.9 ।।
shlokas.transliteration: prajaghne ca nṛpo 'raṇye mṛgāñchatasahasraśaḥ | hatvaiva tṛptirnābhūcca rājñastasya mahātmanaḥ || 7.87.9 ||
shlokas.wordByWord: And the king slew deer in the forest by the hundreds of thousands; yet even by such slaughter no satisfaction came to that great-souled king.

shlokas.sanskrit: नानामृगाणामयुतं वध्यमानं महात्मना । यत्र जातो माहासेनस्तं देशमुपचक्रमे ।। 7.87.10 ।।
shlokas.transliteration: nānāmṛgāṇāmayutaṃ vadhyamānaṃ mahātmanā | yatra jāto māhāsenastaṃ deśamupacakrame || 7.87.10 ||
shlokas.wordByWord: Slaying a myriad of the various wild beasts, that great-souled one came upon that region where Mahasena (Kartikeya) had been born.

shlokas.sanskrit: तस्मिन्प्रदेशे देवेश शैलराजसुतां हरः । रमयामास दुर्धर्षः सर्वैरनुचरैः सह ।। 7.87.11 ।।
shlokas.transliteration: tasminpradeśe deveśa śailarājasutāṃ haraḥ | ramayāmāsa durdharṣaḥ sarvairanucaraiḥ saha || 7.87.11 ||
shlokas.wordByWord: In that region, O lord, Hara, the unassailable one, was disporting himself with the daughter of the mountain-king (Parvati), together with all his attendants.

shlokas.sanskrit: कृत्वा स्त्रीरूपमात्मानमुमेशो गोपतिध्वजः । देव्याः प्रियचिकीर्षुः संस्तस्मिन्पर्वतनिर्झरे ।। 7.87.12 ।।
shlokas.transliteration: kṛtvā strīrūpamātmānamumeśo gopatidhvajaḥ | devyāḥ priyacikīrṣuḥ saṃstasminparvatanirjhare || 7.87.12 ||
shlokas.wordByWord: Wishing to please the goddess, the lord of Uma, whose banner bears the bull, had made himself into the form of a woman there, in that mountain cascade.

shlokas.sanskrit: ये तु तत्र वनोद्देशे सत्त्वाः पुरुषवादिनः । वृक्षाः पुरुषनामानस्ते ऽभवन् स्त्रीजनास्तदा ।। 7.87.13 ।।
shlokas.transliteration: ye tu tatra vanoddeśe sattvāḥ puruṣavādinaḥ | vṛkṣāḥ puruṣanāmānaste 'bhavan strījanāstadā || 7.87.13 ||
shlokas.wordByWord: And whatever beings in that tract of the forest were of male nature, and the trees that bore masculine names, all then became women.

shlokas.sanskrit: यच्च किञ्चन तत्सर्वं नारीसञ्ज्ञं बभूव ह । एतस्मिन्नन्तरे राजा स इलः कर्दमात्मजः । निघ्नन्मृगसहस्राणि तं देशमुपचक्रमे ।। 7.87.14 ।।
shlokas.transliteration: yacca kiñcana tatsarvaṃ nārīsañjñaṃ babhūva ha | etasminnantare rājā sa ilaḥ kardamātmajaḥ | nighnanmṛgasahasrāṇi taṃ deśamupacakrame || 7.87.14 ||
shlokas.wordByWord: Indeed whatever existed there, all of it took on a feminine character. In the meantime that king Ila, the son of Kardama, slaying deer by the thousands, came upon that region.

shlokas.sanskrit: स दृष्ट्वा स्त्रीकृतं सर्वं सव्यालमृगपक्षकम् । आत्मनं स्त्रीकृतं चैव सानुगं रघुनन्दन ।। 7.87.15 ।।
shlokas.transliteration: sa dṛṣṭvā strīkṛtaṃ sarvaṃ savyālamṛgapakṣakam | ātmanaṃ strīkṛtaṃ caiva sānugaṃ raghunandana || 7.87.15 ||
shlokas.wordByWord: When he saw that everything — together with the serpents, beasts, and birds — had been turned into female form, and that he himself along with his followers had been turned into a woman, O delight of the Raghus —

shlokas.sanskrit: तस्य दुःखं महच्चासीद्दृष्ट्वा ऽ ऽत्मानं तथागतम् । उमापतेश्च तत्कर्म ज्ञात्वा त्रासमुपागमत् ।। 7.87.16 ।।
shlokas.transliteration: tasya duḥkhaṃ mahaccāsīddṛṣṭvā ' 'tmānaṃ tathāgatam | umāpateśca tatkarma jñātvā trāsamupāgamat || 7.87.16 ||
shlokas.wordByWord: Great was his grief when he beheld himself reduced to such a state; and when he understood that this was the work of Uma's lord, he was seized with terror.

shlokas.sanskrit: ततो देवं महात्मानं शितिकण्ठं कपर्दिनम् । जगाम शरणं राजा सभृत्यबलवाहनः ।। 7.87.17 ।।
shlokas.transliteration: tato devaṃ mahātmānaṃ śitikaṇṭhaṃ kapardinam | jagāma śaraṇaṃ rājā sabhṛtyabalavāhanaḥ || 7.87.17 ||
shlokas.wordByWord: Then the king, together with his servants, his army, and his mounts, went for refuge to the great-souled god, the white-necked one who wears matted locks.

shlokas.sanskrit: ततः प्रहस्य वरदः सह देव्या महेश्वरः । प्रजापतिसुतं वाक्यमुवाच वरदः स्वयम् ।। 7.87.18 ।।
shlokas.transliteration: tataḥ prahasya varadaḥ saha devyā maheśvaraḥ | prajāpatisutaṃ vākyamuvāca varadaḥ svayam || 7.87.18 ||
shlokas.wordByWord: Thereupon the great lord Maheshvara, the bestower of boons, laughing along with his consort, himself the giver of boons, spoke these words to the son of Prajapati.

shlokas.sanskrit: उत्तिष्ठोत्तिष्ठ राजर्षे कार्दमेय महाबल । पुरुषत्वमृते सौम्य वरं वरय सुव्रत ।। 7.87.19 ।।
shlokas.transliteration: uttiṣṭhottiṣṭha rājarṣe kārdameya mahābala | puruṣatvamṛte saumya varaṃ varaya suvrata || 7.87.19 ||
shlokas.wordByWord: "Rise up, rise up, O royal sage, O mighty son of Kardama! Except for manhood, O gentle one, O you of firm vows, choose whatever boon you desire."

shlokas.sanskrit: ततः स राजा दुःखार्तः प्रत्याख्यातो महात्मना । न च जग्राह स्त्रीभूतो वरमन्यं सुरोत्तमात् ।। 7.87.20 ।।
shlokas.transliteration: tataḥ sa rājā duḥkhārtaḥ pratyākhyāto mahātmanā | na ca jagrāha strībhūto varamanyaṃ surottamāt || 7.87.20 ||
shlokas.wordByWord: Then the king, tormented by grief and refused by the great-souled god, being turned into a woman, did not accept any other boon from that best of the gods.

shlokas.sanskrit: ततः शोकेन महता शैलराजसुतां नृपः । प्रणिपत्य ह्युमां देवीं सर्वेणैवान्तरात्मना ।। 7.87.21 ।।
shlokas.transliteration: tataḥ śokena mahatā śailarājasutāṃ nṛpaḥ | praṇipatya hyumāṃ devīṃ sarveṇaivāntarātmanā || 7.87.21 ||
shlokas.wordByWord: Then, with great sorrow, the king bowed down with his whole inmost being before the goddess Uma, daughter of the mountain-king.

shlokas.sanskrit: ईशे वराणां वरदे लोकानामसि भामिनी । अमोघदर्शने देवी भज सौम्येन चक्षुषा ।। 7.87.22 ।।
shlokas.transliteration: īśe varāṇāṃ varade lokānāmasi bhāminī | amoghadarśane devī bhaja saumyena cakṣuṣā || 7.87.22 ||
shlokas.wordByWord: "O mistress, O bestower of boons, O radiant one, you are the giver of boons to the worlds; O goddess whose glance is never in vain, look upon me with a kindly eye."

shlokas.sanskrit: हृद्गतं तस्य राजर्षेर्विज्ञाय हरसन्निधौ । प्रत्युवाच शुभं वाक्यं देवी रुद्रस्य संमता ।। 7.87.23 ।।
shlokas.transliteration: hṛdgataṃ tasya rājarṣervijñāya harasannidhau | pratyuvāca śubhaṃ vākyaṃ devī rudrasya saṃmatā || 7.87.23 ||
shlokas.wordByWord: Perceiving what was in the heart of that royal sage there in Hara's presence, the goddess, who was honored by Rudra, replied with auspicious words.

shlokas.sanskrit: अर्धस्य देवो वरदो वरार्धस्य तव ह्यहम् । तस्मादर्धं गृहाण त्वं स्त्रीपुंसोर्यावदिच्छसि ।। 7.87.24 ।।
shlokas.transliteration: ardhasya devo varado varārdhasya tava hyaham | tasmādardhaṃ gṛhāṇa tvaṃ strīpuṃsoryāvadicchasi || 7.87.24 ||
shlokas.wordByWord: "The god is the bestower of one half of the boon, and I indeed am the bestower of the other half; therefore take from your half as much of womanhood or manhood as you wish."

shlokas.sanskrit: तदद्भुततरं श्रुत्वा देव्या वरमनुत्तमम् । सम्प्रहृष्टमना भूत्वा राजा वाक्यमथाब्रवीत् ।। 7.87.25 ।।
shlokas.transliteration: tadadbhutataraṃ śrutvā devyā varamanuttamam | samprahṛṣṭamanā bhūtvā rājā vākyamathābravīt || 7.87.25 ||
shlokas.wordByWord: Hearing that most wondrous and unsurpassed boon of the goddess, the king, his mind filled with delight, then spoke these words.

shlokas.sanskrit: यदि देवि प्रसन्ना मे रूपेणाप्रतिमा भुवि । मासं स्त्रीत्वमुपासित्वा मासं स्यां पुरुषः पुनः ।। 7.87.26 ।।
shlokas.transliteration: yadi devi prasannā me rūpeṇāpratimā bhuvi | māsaṃ strītvamupāsitvā māsaṃ syāṃ puruṣaḥ punaḥ || 7.87.26 ||
shlokas.wordByWord: "O goddess, if you are pleased with me, then let me, unequalled in beauty upon the earth, dwell in womanhood for a month and then again become a man for a month."

shlokas.sanskrit: ईप्सितं तस्य विज्ञाय देवी सुरुचिरानना । प्रत्युवाच शुभं वाक्यमेवमेव भविष्यति ।। 7.87.27 ।।
shlokas.transliteration: īpsitaṃ tasya vijñāya devī surucirānanā | pratyuvāca śubhaṃ vākyamevameva bhaviṣyati || 7.87.27 ||
shlokas.wordByWord: Understanding what he desired, the goddess of lovely countenance replied with auspicious words: "So shall it be."

shlokas.sanskrit: राजन्पुरुषभूतस्त्वं स्त्रीभावं न स्मरिष्यसि । स्त्रीभूतश्च परं मासं न स्मरिष्यसि पौरुषम् ।। 7.87.28 ।।
shlokas.transliteration: rājanpuruṣabhūtastvaṃ strībhāvaṃ na smariṣyasi | strībhūtaśca paraṃ māsaṃ na smariṣyasi pauruṣam || 7.87.28 ||
shlokas.wordByWord: "O king, when you are a man you shall not remember your state as a woman, and when you have become a woman, for that whole month you shall not remember your manhood."

shlokas.sanskrit: एवं स राजा पुरुषो मासं भूत्वाथ कार्दमिः । त्रैलोक्यसुन्दरी नारी मासमेकमिला ऽभवत् ।। 7.87.29 ।।
shlokas.transliteration: evaṃ sa rājā puruṣo māsaṃ bhūtvātha kārdamiḥ | trailokyasundarī nārī māsamekamilā 'bhavat || 7.87.29 ||
shlokas.wordByWord: Thus that king, the son of Kardama, having become a man for one month, then for one month became Ila, a woman beautiful beyond all the three worlds.

shlokas.sanskrit: इत्यार्षे श्रीमद्रामायणे वाल्मीकीये आदिकाव्ये श्रीमदुत्तरकाण्डे सप्ताशीतितमः सर्गः ।। 87 ।।
shlokas.transliteration: ityārṣe śrīmadrāmāyaṇe vālmīkīye ādikāvye śrīmaduttarakāṇḍe saptāśītitamaḥ sargaḥ || 87 ||
shlokas.wordByWord: Thus ends the eighty-seventh canto in the venerable Uttara Kanda of the holy Ramayana, the first epic poem composed by the sage Valmiki.
